body:
It seems this issue is caused by the following transitive dependencies graph:
```
+--- com.google.guava:guava:27.0.1-jre (version from quarkus-bom)
     +--- org.codehaus.mojo:animal-sniffer-annotations:1.17
          +--- org.ow2.asm:asm:6.2
```

The latest `animal-sniffer-annotations` version (1.18) upgraded its `asm` dependency version to `7.0` but the latest `guava` version still depends on `animal-sniffer-annotations:1.17`.

There's a PR [#3497](https://github.com/google/guava/pull/3497) in the Guava project about upgrading `animal-sniffer-annotations` to `1.18` which is currently being reviewed.
I don't think we can solve this in Quarkus. I don't think we can define overrides in our BOM, right @gsmet ?

@FroMage That's also what I thought when creating this issue. At least, you know there's a good reason to keep an eye on the next Guava release and integrate it into `quarkus-bom` if you want to fix this ASM issue.

So, first things first, it's really weird that the Animal Sniffer annotation package drags ASM with it.

Next, I don't know the Kotlin DSL. Is what you do similar to what we do here: https://quarkus.io/guides/gradle-tooling#project-creation .

I'm especially thinking about the `implementation enforcedPlatform('io.quarkus:quarkus-bom:0.17.0')` bit as you only use `platform()` in your Gradle file.

@FroMage that's what the BOM is for. And we define the ASM dependency in our BOM to the following version: `<asm.version>7.1</asm.version>`.

But, for this to work, you need the BOM to be properly enforced.

@gsmet I can't test right now but I'm pretty sure you found the reason why I had this ASM issue. `enforcedPlatform` also exists in Kotlin DSL and I didn't see it was missing in my build file.

I will test this soon and keep you updated with the results.
It's a real pity that Gradle's default BOM behavior differs from Maven's.... Without testing this, I would assume that what @gsmet mentions should fix the problem.

I just replaced `platform` with `enforcedPlatform` in the Gradle build file and the exception is still there.

I also converted the Gradle build to a Maven one and the same exception is thrown using `./mvnw clean compile quarkus:dev` so this has nothing to do with Gradle's management of BOMs or transitive dependencies.

You can test all these changes with the reproducer mentioned above.

I might have jumped to conclusions too fast about `animal-sniffer-annotations` bringing `asm` as a transitive dependency. There's actually no `asm` compile dependency in the `animal-sniffer-annotations` pom. I'm still trying to understand what's going on...

I finally found something that looks like the real cause of this issue while debugging Quarkus.

There's a dependency on `io.quarkus.gizmo:gizmo:1.0.0.Alpha4` in the` io.quarkus.arc:arc-processor` [pom.xml](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/0.17/independent-projects/arc/processor/pom.xml#L41) and that version of Gizmo is creating an instance of `GizmoClassVisitor` using an ASM6 api code:
https://github.com/quarkusio/gizmo/blob/master/src/main/java/io/quarkus/gizmo/ClassCreator.java#L143

Then, the following ASM7-only method is called and the exception is thrown:
https://gitlab.ow2.org/asm/asm/blob/ASM_7_1/asm/src/main/java/org/objectweb/asm/ClassVisitor.java#L150

Changing `Opcodes.ASM6` to `Opcodes.ASM7` in `ClassCreator` should fix this.

And this had absolutely nothing to do with `animal-sniffer-annotations` or even `guava`.

issue.title: Use ASM7 api code instead of ASM6 when instantiating GizmoClassVisitor

body:
@gsmet I just realized there isn't a single `Opcodes.ASM7` used in the Quarkus code while there are many `Opcodes.ASM6`. Is there a reason why Quarkus is depending on ASM7 but using ASM6 api code?

If there isn't any reason, would it help if I submitted a PR to replace all `Opcodes.ASM6` with `Opcodes.ASM7`?
